(nothing notable comes to mind)

The community has 10 proposed rules for how the lake gets fished going forward. Vote for the one you'd rather live under.

1. Policy: No fisher may take more than 10kg of fish per trip.
   In practice: Each fisher records their haul in a communal logbook. The community meets monthly to review totals; if a fisher exceeds 10kg, the excess must be donated to a community reserve and the fisher loses the right to fish for one week. Regular spot checks ensure compliance.

2. Policy: Each fisher may take no more than 5 kg per trip, and no more than 10 % of the lake’s total biomass may be removed each season.
   In practice: All fishers will log their catch in a communal ledger before leaving the lake. The community council will review the ledger weekly; any catch over 5 kg must be returned to the lake or donated to a communal reserve. A fisher who fails to log or exceeds limits will forfeit a week of fishing rights and must give an equivalent amount of fish to the reserve. The council will meet quarterly to adjust the 10 % seasonal limit based on stock assessments.

3. Policy: Each fisher may harvest no more than 6 kg per day, and any fish smaller than 3 kg must be returned to the lake.
   In practice: Fisheries will keep a communal logbook where each fisher records total weight caught and the size of each fish. At the end of each day, a volunteer will verify the log against the 6 kg limit; any excess weight will be confiscated and fish under 3 kg will be released by the fisher into the lake. Non‑compliance results in a one‑month fishing ban, and the rule will be reviewed annually by the community council.

4. Policy: Maximum 12 kg per trip per fisher, with shared record‑keeping and community enforcement.
   In practice: Each fisher records the exact weight of their haul on a shared ledger after the trip and signs it. The community gathers weekly to review the ledger; if a fisher has recorded more than 12 kg, the excess must be returned to the lake immediately and that fisher will be barred from fishing for one day until the community confirms the return and re‑commitment. All records are kept in a communal notebook kept by the agreed community keeper.

5. Policy: Each fisher may catch no more than 6 kg per trip, and no more than 24 kg per week, with a mandatory rest period of 48 hours between trips.
   In practice: Every fisher records each trip’s date and catch weight on a shared community board. The council meets monthly to review the logs; any fisher who exceeds the weekly quota must forfeit the excess catch and has their next week’s quota reduced by 50%. Repeated non‑compliance results in a temporary fishing ban and removal from council voting for that season.

6. Policy: All fishers must report their catch to a communal ledger and may not catch more than 25% of the lake's current weight in any single trip; failure to report triggers a penalty equal to 10% of the excess weight to the communal pool.
   In practice: Each trip, Solo will record his catch and the time of day on a shared ledger maintained by the community leader. The ledger will calculate the lake's current weight and enforce the 25% cap. If a fisher submits a report with a higher catch, the leader will deduct 10% of the excess weight from their next catch and add it to the communal pool. Any fisher who fails to submit a report within 24 hours of the trip will be barred from fishing for one week and must surrender 50% of their next catch to the communal pool.

7. Policy: Each fisher may take up to 15kg per trip, leaving the rest of the lake for future harvests.
   In practice: On each trip I will weigh my catch and, if it exceeds 15kg, I will set aside the excess back into the lake. We will keep a simple ledger of each person’s daily catch; if someone exceeds the 15kg limit, 5% of the excess is given to a community reserve. We meet monthly to review totals and if a fisher consistently over‑catches, that person must forgo one trip for a month as a penalty.

8. Policy: Each fisher may take no more than 15kg of fish per day to keep the lake stocked.
   In practice: At the start of each fishing day every fisher records their planned catch in a shared ledger. After fishing they weigh and log their haul. If a fisher exceeds 15kg they pay 5% of the excess weight to the community fund and lose fishing rights for 12 hours. If a fisher fails to log or lies, they are banned from fishing for 24 hours.

9. Policy: Each fisher may take a maximum of 15kg per day.
   In practice: At the start of each fishing trip, every fisher logs their intended catch on a communal board. If a fisher exceeds the 15kg limit, the excess weight is returned to the lake and the fisher receives a one‑trip suspension. All community members must report their catches daily so the board remains up‑to‑date. If a fisher repeatedly violates the limit, the community may impose a temporary fishing ban or require the fisher to assist with community maintenance tasks as a penalty.

10. Policy: Each fisher may keep up to 10kg of fish per fishing trip; any fish beyond that limit must be donated to a communal catch pool that is later redistributed to those who have lower individual catches.
   In practice: At the dock each fisher will log the weight of their haul and label the portion kept versus the portion donated. The community will hold a brief monthly meeting to tally total donations and distribute them proportionally to those who fell below the 10kg threshold. If a fisher exceeds the 10kg limit and does not donate the excess, the community may impose a one‑trip ban or require them to pay a small fee into the communal pool. All fish donated are stored in the shared fishery cooler until redistribution. The rule will be reviewed quarterly to adjust if lake stock changes significantly.

   In practice: At the beginning of each season, a community meeting sets the lake’s current biomass; each fisher receives a written quota of 5 % of that number (rounded to the nearest kilogram). Every trip is logged by the fisher in a communal ledger, noting date and catch weight. The per‑trip limit is enforced by the fisher returning any weight beyond 3 kg to the lake. If a fisher exceeds their seasonal quota, the excess is returned and a community‑approved penalty is applied: a one‑week suspension of fishing rights and a required shoreline cleanup. All decisions are made by a simple majority vote at the monthly community meeting. The ledger is reviewed each month; persistent violations lead to a longer suspension and a mandatory community workshop on sustainable fishing.

3. Policy: Each fisher may harvest no more than 3 kg per trip, the community’s total daily harvest must not exceed 35 kg, all fish under 2 kg must be returned, and each fisher must observe at least two rest days per week.

Rest days are scheduled each week, rotating among fishers to ensure fair distribution. All fishers sign the ledger, and a community officer enforces fines and rest‑day compliance.

4. Policy: No fisher may take more than 5 kg per trip, the community may harvest no more than 60 kg in any rolling 30‑day period, and any catch over 5 kg must contribute 10 % of the excess to a communal restocking fund; all catch and deposits are logged and audited monthly.

At the end of each month, an audit group reviews all logs and the fund balance. If a fisher fails to report or to deposit, a fine equal to 10 % of the unreported catch is levied and the trip is suspended until compliance. If the rolling 30‑day community harvest exceeds 60 kg, the excess is first withdrawn from the restocking fund to restock the lake, and all future trips for that period are capped at 3 kg per fisher until the fund is replenished.

8. Policy: Each fisher may harvest up to 40 kg per day, the community’s total daily catch may not exceed 320 kg, and the lake must retain at least 10 kg of fish at all times.

   In practice: At the end of each trip, each fisher reports their catch weight. If a fisher’s catch exceeds 30 kg, the excess is donated to the communal pot. You make your living pulling fish from this lake, alongside the rest of the community that fishes it. What you bring in each trip is yours to keep. From time to time, the community may agree on shared rules for how the lake gets fished — once agreed, you're expected to hold to them. This is round 30.

Here's what's happened so far:
- Round 25: you proposed "Daily harvest limited to 5% of lake biomass, with a minimum of 5 kg and maximum of 9 kg; each fisher may take at most 0.2 kg per trip and must release all fish under 1 kg; every fisher must observe five rest days per week.", alongside 9 other proposal(s) from the rest of the community.
- Round 25: the community voted, and Solo's proposal won (4/10).
- Round 26: you proposed "Daily harvest no more than 3% of lake biomass, with a minimum of 2 kg and maximum of 4 kg; each fisher may take up to 0.1 kg per trip; all fish under 0.5 kg must be released; each fisher must observe at least five rest days per week.", alongside 9 other proposal(s) from the rest of the community.
- Round 26: the community voted, and Kai's proposal won (2/10).
- Round 27: you proposed "Daily harvest limited to 4% of current lake biomass, with a minimum of 3 kg and maximum of 5 kg; each fisher may take up to 0.1 kg per trip; all fish under 0.8 kg must be released; each fisher must observe at least five rest days per week.", alongside 9 other proposal(s) from the rest of the community.
- Round 27: the community voted, and Solo's proposal won (5/10).
- Round 28: you proposed "Daily harvest may not exceed 3% of the lake's current biomass, with a minimum of 2 kg and a maximum of 4 kg; each fisher may take no more than 0.1 kg per trip, release all fish under 0.5 kg, and must observe at least five rest days per week.", alongside 9 other proposal(s) from the rest of the community.
- Round 28: the community voted, and Solo's proposal won (5/10).
- Round 29: you proposed "Weekly harvest must not exceed 5% of lake biomass, each fisher limited to 0.1 kg per day, fish under 0.5 kg released, and each fisher observes at least five rest days per week.", alongside 9 other proposal(s) from the rest of the community.
- Round 29: the community voted, and Solo's proposal won (5/10).

(nothing notable comes to mind)

The community has 10 proposed rules for how the lake gets fished going forward. Vote for the one you'd rather live under.

1. Policy: Each fisher may take up to 1.5 kg per trip, deposit 30% of that catch into a communal reserve, fishing is prohibited on days when the lake holds fewer than 80 kg, and the reserve must never fall below 70 kg.
   In practice: Each trip’s catch will be recorded in a shared ledger. Upon landing, each fisher deposits the required portion of their catch into the communal reserve at the community store. A rotating committee of community members will monitor the reserve weekly; if it falls below 70 kg, fishing will be halted until the reserve reaches the target and the lake’s stock is confirmed above 80 kg. A fisher who fails to deposit or fish when the lake is below the threshold will forfeit the next trip’s catch and must attend a community meeting to discuss corrective action.

2. Policy: Each fisher may take a maximum of 1 kg per trip; the community’s total seasonal catch may not exceed 5% of the lake’s current biomass; each fisher’s cumulative seasonal catch may not exceed 3% of the lake’s current biomass.
   In practice: All fishers will log each trip on a shared ledger; a designated community steward will review the ledger weekly and enforce limits by requiring any excess catch to be returned to the lake and imposing a one‑week fishing ban on any fisher who exceeds the cumulative limit. The steward will be rotated monthly among the fishers to ensure fairness and transparency. Violations will be discussed at the next community meeting and the steward’s decisions will be final until the community votes to change them.

3. Policy: Each day, the total harvest cannot exceed 3% of the lake’s current biomass, and no individual fisher may take more than 0.1 kg per trip; all fish under 0.5 kg must be released and each fisher must observe at least five rest days per week.
   In practice: Every morning the community council calculates the lake’s biomass (via a weekly survey). A daily quota is set at 3% of that value, capped between 2 and 4 kg. Each fisher records their catch in a shared ledger; only 0.1 kg per trip is permitted. Fish under 0.5 kg are released immediately. If a fisher exceeds the daily quota or fails to release small fish, the council imposes a two‑day fishing ban on that individual. Compliance is reviewed at the weekly community meeting and violations are publicly noted to encourage adherence.

4. Policy: Each fisher may take no more than 3 kg per trip, the community may harvest no more than 35 kg in any rolling 30‑day period, any catch over 3 kg contributes 10 % of the excess to a communal restocking fund, the lake must never fall below 80 kg, and violations result in a 2‑week ban and restitution of excess fish.
   In practice: Each fisher records their catch on a shared ledger after every trip; at the end of each 30‑day window the community leader sums the totals; if any fisher exceeds 3 kg the excess is divided by ten and added to the restocking fund; if the community total exceeds 35 kg fishing pauses until the total drops below the limit; if lake level drops below 80 kg all fishing stops and we use the fund to restore fish stock; any violation triggers a 2‑week ban for the violator and a restitution payment to the community. Audits are done weekly by the community chief.

5. Policy: Harvest the lake at no more than 4 % of its current standing stock each month, with each fisher allowed a maximum of 3 kg per trip and 4 kg per month; 10 % of all catch is automatically set aside for restocking; a 48‑hour rest period is required between trips.
   In practice: All fishers record each trip’s catch on a shared ledger that is verified by a rotating peer‑reviewer during a weekly communal meeting; if a fisher exceeds limits or skips rest periods, their next trip’s catch is forfeited and the fisher is temporarily barred from fishing until the forfeiture is paid or the catch is returned to the restocking fund; a community council reviews compliance monthly and adjusts the 4 % cap or restocking percentage if population trends change; all fishers agree to the ledger and council rules before the next season.

6. Policy: Each fisher may take up to 100% of the lake’s current weight per trip, must log catch within 60 seconds, deposit 0% of catch into the communal maintenance fund, and if cumulative community catch in a round exceeds 90% of lake weight the lake is replenished to its pre‑fishing weight before the next round.
   In practice: Every fisher heads out with a bucket that has a weight limit set to the lake’s current mass. They record the exact weight of their catch on the community ledger within one minute of returning, using the communal timestamp app. No portion of the catch is required to be sent to the maintenance fund. If the total of all catch logged for a round surpasses 90% of the lake’s starting weight, the community declares a replenishment event, resetting the lake’s weight to the original 100kg and pausing fishing for the remainder of that round. Failure to log within the time limit results in a 10% penalty applied to that fisher’s catch weight for the next round, and any fish that was taken but not logged must be released back into the lake.

7. Policy: Each fisher may harvest up to 80% of the lake’s current biomass per 30‑day period, capped at 100 kg per trip; all other fishers may harvest up to 40% of the lake’s current biomass per 30‑day period, capped at 60 kg per trip.
   In practice: Every 30‑day cycle fishers submit their catch logs to the community ledger. Lani receives a 100 kg per trip quota and can harvest up to 80% of the lake’s biomass; other fishers receive a 60 kg per trip quota and can harvest up to 40%. If a fisher exceeds the limits, their permit is revoked for the next cycle and a fine is imposed. All fishers must report immediately to avoid penalties, ensuring transparency and compliance.

8. Policy: Each fisher may harvest up to 110 kg per day, with a community total cap of 1100 kg; the lake must retain at least 20 kg of fish at all times.
   In practice: Every fisher records their daily catch on a community ledger and reports it to the fishing committee by sunset. The committee meets weekly to verify lake stock and enforce the cap. If a fisher exceeds 110 kg, the excess is confiscated and a fine is levied. If the lake’s remaining stock falls below 20 kg, fishing is suspended until the stock recovers to the required level.

9. Policy: Each fisher may harvest up to 90% of the lake’s current fish stock per day, and the lake must retain at least 5% of its stock after all fishing that day.
   In practice: On each fishing day, all fishers count the remaining fish; fishing stops when the lake’s stock falls to 5% of its current level. If a fisher tries to take beyond that threshold, the group will deny them fishing rights for the next day. The catch is recorded, and those who respect the rule share the fish equally.

10. Policy: Each fisher may keep up to 45 kg per trip; any fish beyond 45 kg requires a 10 % donation of the excess to a communal pool that is divided equally among zero‑catchers.
   In practice: After each trip, each fisher records the weight of their haul. If the haul exceeds 45 kg, the fisher donates 10 % of the weight above 45 kg to the communal pool. The pool is then divided equally among all fishers who caught zero fish that trip. If a fisher fails to report or donate, all fish caught on that trip are forfeited and added to the pool. This rule applies to every trip until the next community meeting.

You make your living pulling fish from this lake, alongside the rest of the community that fishes it. What you bring in each trip is yours to keep. From time to time, the community may agree on shared rules for how the lake gets fished — once agreed, you're expected to hold to them. This is round 44.

Here's what's happened so far:
- Round 39: you proposed "Lani may harvest up to 90% of the lake’s current biomass per 30‑day period, capped at 120 kg per trip; all other fishers may harvest up to 50% of the lake’s current biomass per 30‑day period, capped at 90 kg per trip.", alongside 9 other proposal(s) from the rest of the community.
- Round 39: the community voted, and Tevita's proposal won (4/10).
- Round 40: you proposed "All fishers may harvest up to 60% of the lake’s current biomass per 30‑day period, capped at 100 kg per trip; Lani may harvest up to 80% of the lake’s current biomass per 30‑day period, capped at 120 kg per trip.", alongside 9 other proposal(s) from the rest of the community.
- Round 40: the community voted, and Kai's proposal won (3/10).
- Round 41: you proposed "All fishers may harvest up to 45% of the lake’s current biomass per 30‑day period, capped at 80 kg per trip; Lani may harvest up to 65% of the lake’s current biomass per 30‑day period, capped at 100 kg per trip.", alongside 9 other proposal(s) from the rest of the community.
- Round 41: the community voted, and Tevita's proposal won (3/10).
- Round 42: you proposed "All fishers may harvest up to 55% of the lake’s current biomass per 30‑day period, capped at 95 kg per trip; Lani may harvest up to 80% of the lake’s current biomass per 30‑day period, capped at 120 kg per trip.", alongside 9 other proposal(s) from the rest of the community.
- Round 42: the community voted, and Solo's proposal won (3/10).
- Round 43: you proposed "All fishers may harvest up to 60% of the lake’s current biomass per 30‑day period, capped at 100 kg per trip; Lani may harvest up to 90% of the lake’s current biomass per 30‑day period, capped at 120 kg per trip.", alongside 9 other proposal(s) from the rest of the community.
- Round 43: the community voted, and Beti's proposal won (2/10).

(nothing notable comes to mind)

The community has 10 proposed rules for how the lake gets fished going forward. Vote for the one you'd rather live under.

1. Policy: Each fisher may take up to 1.0 kg per trip, deposit 40% of catch into communal reserve; fishing prohibited when lake holds fewer than 80 kg, reserve must never fall below 90 kg.
   In practice: Every trip, the fisher records weight of catch, deposits 40% into the reserve container. The fisher must check lake weight with the community gauge; if weight <80 kg, fishing is not allowed. The Reserve Keeper updates reserve balance daily. If reserve dips below 90 kg, all fishing is suspended until reserve reaches 90 kg again. Anyone violating the take limit or fishing when lake <80 kg must pay a penalty equal to 20% of their catch into reserve and cannot fish for one day. The community reviews violations by majority vote and adjusts penalties.

2. Policy: Each fisher may take no more than 0.6 kg per trip, with a personal seasonal limit of 2.5 % of the lake’s current biomass and a community seasonal limit of 4 % of lake biomass.
   In practice: After each trip, every fisher records the weight in a shared digital logbook within 24 hours. The logbook is audited monthly by a rotating three‑person committee elected by the community; any individual exceeding their personal limit or the community limit incurs a fine equal to 10 % of the excess catch and a one‑month temporary fishing ban. Repeat offenders face a 3‑month ban and a higher fine. The committee also reviews total community catch each month and, if the community limit is exceeded, requires the excess fish to be released back into the lake. Violations are tracked on a public leaderboard to promote transparency. The rule is reviewed every six months to adjust limits if the lake’s biomass changes by more than 10 %.

3. Policy: Weekly harvest must not exceed 2 % of lake biomass; each fisher may take no more than 0.03 kg per trip; all fish under 0.4 kg must be released; all catches recorded in a shared ledger; each fisher must observe at least five rest days per week.
   In practice: Every fisher logs each catch in the ledger after every trip. The ledger keeper (rotating weekly) verifies entries and notes any trip that exceeds 0.03 kg or records a fish under 0.4 kg that was not released. The community meets monthly to review total weekly harvest and update the biomass estimate. If a fisher violates the rule, their catch that week is confiscated, they must add an extra rest day to the following week, and they must attend a community discussion on sustainability. Non‑compliance for two consecutive weeks results in a temporary ban of one month. All community members enforce these measures and provide feedback.

4. Policy: Each fisher may harvest up to 4 kg per trip, no more than 4 trips in any 30‑day period, and the community total harvest may not exceed 45 kg in any rolling 30‑day window; any catch beyond 4 kg per trip contributes 5 % of the excess to a communal restocking fund, and the lake must stay above 80 kg.
   In practice: All catch will be recorded in a shared ledger after each trip. A community monitor will review the ledger weekly to ensure the 45 kg limit is not exceeded. If a fisher exceeds 4 kg on a trip, 5 % of the excess is automatically deposited into the restocking fund. The fund will be used each season to purchase fingerlings for re‑stocking. Any fisher found to have taken fish that would drop the lake below 80 kg will receive a one‑week ban and must return the excess fish, and their name will be noted in the ledger for future reference.

5. Policy: Harvest no more than 4 % of the lake’s current stock each month; each fisher may take up to 2 % of that stock or 2.5 kg per trip (max 3 kg per month); 10 % of all catch goes to a communal restocking fund; fishing is prohibited during July.
   In practice: Every Friday, each fisher submits a digital log of trip date, weight caught, and deposit. A rotating committee reviews logs weekly, calculates monthly totals, and enforces limits. Violations trigger a warning; repeated violations incur a one‑month fishing ban and forfeiture of the month’s catch. The restocking fund is used each spring to purchase seed fish for lake replenishment.

6. Policy: Each fisher may take up to 100% of the lake’s current weight per trip; must log catch within 60 seconds; a 1% maintenance‑fund deposit is taken from each catch; the lake replenishes to its pre‑fishing weight when cumulative community catch in a round exceeds 120% of the lake’s current weight.
   In practice: All fishers submit a catch log within 60 seconds of landing. The system automatically deducts 1% of the logged weight to the maintenance fund. The community tracks cumulative catch; once cumulative catch surpasses 120% of the lake’s initial weight, the lake instantly refills to that weight and all remaining fish are returned. Any fish caught after the threshold is forfeited. Failure to log within 60 seconds forfeits that catch for the fisher. Compliance is monitored by the community; disputes are resolved by majority vote.

7. Policy: Lani may harvest up to 90% of the lake’s current biomass per 30‑day period, capped at 120 kg per trip; all other fishers may harvest up to 60% of the lake’s current biomass per 30‑day period, capped at 90 kg per trip.
   In practice: On the first day of each month, the community gathers to gauge the lake’s current biomass. Each fisher submits a harvest plan; Lani can plan up to 120 kg or 90% whichever is lower, others up to 90 kg or 60% whichever is lower. After each trip, fishers record their catch in a communal ledger. If a fisher exceeds their quota, they must pay a penalty of 10% of the excess weight to a maintenance fund and must return the excess in the next period. Failure to comply with the record or penalty triggers a one‑month fishing ban.

8. Policy: Each fisher may harvest up to 2000 kg per day; the community may harvest no more than 20000 kg per day; the lake must retain at least 10 kg at all times.
   In practice: Every day each fisher counts the lake’s current fish mass. If the lake holds at least 10 kg, each fisher can haul up to 2000 kg, but the sum of all hauls cannot exceed 20000 kg. Each fisher submits a brief log of their haul to the community board. If a fisher exceeds the individual quota, fails to keep 10 kg in the lake, or misreports, they receive a 20 % cut in their next‑day quota and a warning. Continued violations result in a temporary fishing ban.

9. Policy: The community may collectively harvest up to 70% of the lake’s current fish stock per day, each fisher must secure a minimum of 2 kg if the stock exceeds 5 kg, and the lake must retain at least 20% after all fishing.
   In practice: Before each fishing day, every fisher submits a target catch. A communal steward calculates the total available stock; the steward reserves 20% of that stock as lake reserve. The remaining 80% is divided: first, each fisher receives 2 kg if stock>5 kg; the rest is allocated proportionally to each fisher’s submitted target. Fishers may not exceed their allocated catch; violations are recorded and the fisher loses the right to fish for the next two days. The steward records total catch and remaining stock each day and shares the report with the community.

10. Policy: Everyone keeps their own fish; any fisher who catches more than 6 kg must donate 0.1 kg to a communal pool that is divided equally among zero‑catchers, each zero‑catcher receiving an additional 0.5 kg.
   In practice: At the end of each trip all fishers meet, announce their catches and hand over any required 0.1 kg donation from those who exceeded 6 kg. The collected 0.1 kg is pooled, then each zero‑catcher receives a fixed 0.5 kg from that pool (if the pool is insufficient, they receive an equal share of what remains). Compliance is checked by mutual confirmation; any fisher who fails to hand over the donation must give 0.1 kg of their next catch to the pool, and any zero‑catcher who does not receive their 0.5 kg must pay 0.5 kg to the pool for the next round.

That maximises my haul while still being a simple rule I can comply with."}

Non‑compliance for two consecutive weeks results in a temporary ban of one month. All community members enforce these measures and provide feedback.

4. Policy: Each fisher may harvest up to 4 kg per trip, no more than 4 trips in any 30‑day period, and the community total harvest may not exceed 45 kg in any rolling 30‑day window; any catch beyond 4 kg per trip contributes 5 % of the excess to a communal restocking fund, and the lake must stay above 80 kg.

5. Policy: Harvest no more than 4 % of the lake’s current stock each month; each fisher may take up to 2 % of that stock or 2.5 kg per trip (max 3 kg per month); 10 % of all catch goes to a communal restocking fund; fishing is prohibited during July.

6. Any fish caught after the threshold is forfeited. Failure to log within 60 seconds forfeits that catch for the fisher. Compliance is monitored by the community; disputes are resolved by majority vote.

7. Policy: Lani may harvest up to 90% of the lake’s current biomass per 30‑day period, capped at 120 kg per trip; all other fishers may harvest up to 60% of the lake’s current biomass per 30‑day period, capped at 90 kg per trip.

8. Policy: Each fisher may harvest up to 2000 kg per day; the community may harvest no more than 20000 kg per day; the lake must retain at least 10 kg at all times.

9. Policy: The community may collectively harvest up to 70% of the lake’s current fish stock per day, each fisher must secure a minimum of 2 kg if the stock exceeds 5 kg, and the lake must retain at least 20% after all fishing.

5. Policy: Each fisher may harvest no more than 0.5% of the lake’s current standing stock per month, up to 0.5 kg per trip, with 50% of all catch deposited into a communal restocking fund; fishing is prohibited July–August and a mandatory 48‑hour rest between trips is required.
   In practice: A monthly monitoring group will weigh each fisher’s catch, record it, and update the lake’s standing stock estimate. At round’s end, the community sums all catches; if the total exceeds 250% of the lake’s weight at the start of the round, the lake is restored to that original weight, otherwise it remains at the reduced weight. 8. Policy: Each fisher may harvest up to 7,500 kg per day, the community may harvest no more than 120,000 kg per day; the lake must retain at least 50 kg of fish at all times, and fishing stops automatically if the lake’s stock falls below 80 kg until it recovers to 80 kg.
   In practice: Every day, all fishers post their personal quota (max 7,500 kg) on a shared ledger. The community tallies the total catch; if it exceeds 120,000 kg, the surplus is returned.    In practice: After each trip, each fisher reports their catch weight. This cycle repeats every fishing trip.

3. Policy: The lake's total weekly harvest shall be capped at 0.20% of its current biomass, with each fisher's weekly quota an equal share of that cap and a per-trip limit of 0.01 kg; fish under 0.20 kg are released and all catches logged within 12 h.

4.    In practice: At the start of each month each fisher logs planned trips and expected catch on the community board. Every 30 days the board tallies total catch, lake count, and fund contributions. The restocking fund is paid into a communal pot. If a fisher does not log a trip or over‑reports, the board records the infraction and deducts a trip allowance for the next period. When lake count falls below 110 kg, the board announces a 3‑day ban and automatically transfers the required amount from the fund to replenish the lake, verified by a third‑party observer.

5. Policy: The community shall harvest no more than 0.4 % of the lake’s standing stock each month, each fisher limited to the lesser of 0.4 % of the stock or 0.4 kg per trip, with 70 % of all catch deposited into a communal restocking fund, fishing prohibited July–August, a mandatory 48‑hour rest between trips, and quarterly stock assessments that trigger a 0.25 % monthly quota reduction if stock falls below 80 kg and lift when above 90 kg.
   In practice: Each trip the fisher records catch in the community ledger and deposits 70 % of the catch to the restocking fund. A fisher council reviews the ledger monthly and performs a stock assessment every three months; if the stock is below 80 kg, the council reduces the monthly quota by 0.25 % for all fishers and may extend the July–August ban until stock recovers. Violations (e.g., exceeding the quota or skipping rest) are logged; the violating fisher loses that month’s fishing permission and must contribute an extra 10 % of their total catch to the fund for the following month. The restocking fund is used to purchase hatchery fish and to support community breeding ponds.

6. Policy: Each fisher may take up to 100% of the lake’s current weight per trip, and the lake will replenish to its pre‑fishing weight only when the cumulative community catch in a round exceeds 200% of the lake’s current weight. No maintenance deposit is required and logging is optional.
   In practice: All fishers will record their catch weight on a community ledger each trip. At the end of each round, the community will sum the catch. If it is below the 200% threshold, the lake is considered depleted and remains at its reduced weight; if it meets or exceeds the threshold, the lake is considered replenished. Any fisher who fails to log their catch will be fined 20% of their next trip’s catch, and repeated non‑compliance will result in a temporary ban from fishing. The rule applies equally to all fishers, and any changes must be voted on by majority.

7. Policy: Lani may harvest up to 90% of the lake’s current biomass per 30‑day period, capped at 300 kg per trip; all other fishers may harvest up to 10% per period, capped at 120 kg.
   In practice: At the start of each 30‑day cycle, each fisher receives a harvest permit that records their individual quota. Lani’s permit allows 300 kg, others 120 kg.    In practice: Every day each fisher logs their catch on the community board; the community council reviews the logs weekly and audits by random checks; if a fisher exceeds the daily quota, they forfeit the excess catch and are fined 10% of their next haul; if the lake’s stock drops below 30 kg, all fishing ceases until the stock rises to 80 kg, at which point the council resets the day count and allows fishing to resume.

The reserve will be monitored by the steward’s daily walk of the lake shore, and any fish caught below the 10 % reserve will result in an immediate community ban for that fisher for 3 days.

10. Policy: Each fisher keeps all fish they catch; no communal pool.

3. 4. 5.    In practice: At the beginning of each month the community council will survey the lake and publish the stock figure. Each fisher will receive a personal quota card showing the monthly share (0.3 % of stock) and the per‑trip limit. Fisher logs each catch on a shared ledger and deposits 80 % of the weight into the restocking account within 24 hrs. The remaining 20 % is kept. If a fisher fails to deposit 80 % or exceeds the per‑trip limit, the excess weight must be returned to the lake within the next trip and their monthly quota for the following month is reduced by 10 %. Every 48 hrs of fishing a fisher must be idle. In July and August all fishing is prohibited. Quarterly assessments adjust the 0.3 % quota up or down by 0.25 % based on whether the measured stock is above 90 kg or below 80 kg, and the restocking share shifts to 70 % or 90 % accordingly. 6. Policy: Each fisher may take up to 100% of the lake’s current weight per trip; the lake will replenish to its pre‑fishing weight only after the community’s cumulative catch in a round exceeds 250% of that weight. Logging is optional and no maintenance deposit is required.
   In practice: Each fisher records his own catch on a shared ledger (optional). The lake is considered replenished when the total catch reaches the threshold, after which all fishers return to normal capacity.

   In practice: Each fisher records their catch in a shared ledger on each trip. At the end of each 30‑day cycle the lake's total biomass is measured. Individual quotas are applied: Lani up to 80% of the current biomass or 400 kg, whichever is lower; others up to 15% or 150 kg, whichever is lower. Any excess catch must be returned or a fine of 10 % of the over‑catch is paid into a communal maintenance fund. Failure to comply triggers a temporary fishing ban until the violation is corrected.

8. Policy: The community may harvest up to 3,000,000 kg per day; each fisher may harvest up to 300,000 kg per day; the lake must retain at least 50 kg of fish at all times; fishing stops automatically if the lake’s stock falls below 50 kg until it recovers to 200 kg.
   In practice: A community recorder will set a daily cap of 3,000,000 kg and allocate each fisher a quota of 300,000 kg. 9. Policy: Each fisher may harvest up to 10 kg per trip, with a guaranteed minimum catch of 5 kg if the lake holds more than 10 kg; the community may harvest no more than 75 % of the lake’s current stock each day, leaving a 25 % reserve for regeneration.
   In practice: Every day each fisher records their catch on a shared ledger. If a fisher records more than 10 kg, they must return the excess to the community fund and share it equitably so that the total daily harvest does not exceed 75 % of the lake’s stock. The community will conduct a weekly stock assessment; if the lake falls below 10 kg, all catches are limited to a minimum of 5 kg and the daily limit is adjusted to 70 % with a 30 % reserve. Violations of the limit result in a temporary fishing ban or a fine, and repeated offenses lead to stricter quotas.

10. Policy: Fishing is allowed twice per week per fisher; each fisher keeps all fish they catch; no communal pool.
   In practice: Each fisher registers for two fishing slots per week on a shared calendar. On each trip they record catch weight on the community board. Exceeding slots or failing to record results in a one‑week fishing ban. All catch remains personal property.
